statusText: Tail risk is in the low band at 9% while Stress remains high at 75%. Mapped policy state: EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is well below the 25% block threshold because the observed Sunday reopen path completed a full retracement back to Friday's settlement rather than extending, so the demanding rate, energy and geopolitical backdrop is expressed through Stress. The 13:00Z-15:00Z US cash-open window on 28 September is flagged as the narrow danger window for conditional opening-auction continuation risk.
headline: Full round trip in Sunday Globex back to Friday's 30,889 settle pulls Tail down to 9%, while $93 WTI, a 5.18% 10-year and an unresolved Hormuz standoff keep Stress at 75%
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are near 30,884-30,896 in the Sunday Globex session, essentially flat against Friday's 30,889.25 settlement, after a two-way path that is the central observation of this assessment. Price pushed to a session high of 30,920.75, was sold to a low of 30,781.75, and has since been bought back to the settlement area; Yahoo Finance and Investing.com quotes taken minutes apart agree on that round trip. A genuine retracement is therefore on the record and no persistent one-way structure has formed, which is why Tail falls from 14% to 9% even though the surrounding backdrop is unchanged. S&P 500 futures near 7,788.75 are 0.19% lower inside a 7,779-7,803 band, an aligned move that offers no evidence of an index-specific dislocation. The backdrop itself remains demanding. WTI crude is $93.20, up about 0.85% and below its $93.60 session high, with Brent above $106, after President Trump rejected Iran's seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Iran restated that it will not soften its conditions. Al Jazeera reports continuing attacks on commercial shipping, a fatality aboard an Indian cargo ship last week, and analyst expectations of controlled attrition rather than immediate escalation. That is a live geopolitical discontinuity risk and the principal reason Stress is held at 75%, but an oil complex repricing by under one percent in thin Sunday liquidity is not evidence of the pathological equity price path that Tail measures. Rates are the second Stress anchor: the Federal Reserve H.15 release for 24 September shows the 2-year at 4.87%, the 10-year at 5.18% and the 30-year at 5.47%, with the 10-year having touched a 19-year high near 5.196% on Friday and the 10-year real yield moving to about 2.85% from 2.44%, after the FOMC raised its target range to 3.75%-4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote. Cash equities nevertheless closed last week higher, with the Nasdaq-100 at 30,608.14, and the VIX settled Friday at 14.87, down 5.11%; no live volatility-futures read is available because the shared context collector again reported its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Its breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections are labelled latest-session, delayed, non-real-time context and show a constructive but widely dispersed Friday tone, with Microsoft up 3.66% and Qualcomm up 3.97% against Meta down 3.33% and Intel down 3.45%. That dispersion is supporting colour for two-way rotation rather than evidence of current NQ structure. Tail therefore sits in the low band at 9% while Stress is held at 75% and Confidence improves to 77% on two independent live futures reads and fresh verified weekend reporting.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours are covered by published Claude assessments. Tail stayed inside the 6%-14% low band throughout, drifting up from 6% across the quiet weekend to 14% at the Sunday futures reopen. Stress climbed steadily from 55% to 76% as the long-end yield and oil backdrop was reassessed through the non-trading window. Confidence eased from 74% to 67% in the thin overnight hours, recovered to 79% as fresh weekend reporting arrived, then settled near 74% in thin reopen liquidity. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green with a normal dominant mode, and no historical opinion has been revised.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 00:00Z hour on 28 September through 23:00Z the same day. Tail is held in the low band for 22 of the 24 hours and lifts to the 20% watch band only for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z US cash-open hours, where unobserved opening-auction continuation is the specific structure of concern. Stress stays in the high band throughout on generational long-end yields, a $93 oil complex, a hiking Fed and an unresolved Hormuz standoff, easing to 70% only at the end of the horizon. Confidence dips through the thin Asian hours and improves as European and then US price discovery arrives. Monday's scheduled catalysts are limited to the Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index and a Barkin speech; the week's high-impact releases, including Core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and Non-Farm Payrolls, fall after this horizon and are held in the events calendar.

forecast.analysis: Observed: the Sunday reopen path is two-way. NQ pushed to 30,920.75, was sold to 30,781.75, and has recovered to about 30,884-30,896, roughly flat against Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. A genuine retracement has occurred, so Tail eases to 9% while a $93 oil complex and a 5.18% 10-year hold Stress high.

forecast.analysis: Early Tokyo hours. Conditional: while the reopen range between 30,781.75 and 30,920.75 continues to contain price, Tail stays in the low band. A decisive break that then refuses to retrace would be the first structure to watch, and nothing of that kind is observed at this point.

forecast.analysis: Tokyo mid-session. Tail is modelled marginally lower because the Sunday risk premium normally decays once the reopen gap has been absorbed. Stress stays high on the standing rate and energy backdrop rather than on any assumed price path for this hour.

Low participation limits the size of structure that can form

forecast.analysis: Tokyo close approaches. Friday's cash session showed constructive but dispersed megacap behaviour, with Microsoft up 3.7% and Qualcomm up 4% against declines elsewhere in the basket. That dispersion argues for two-way rotation rather than index-level one-way risk in this window.
drivers: Friday megacap dispersion: Microsoft +3.7% and Qualcomm +4% against decliners

drivers: Asia-to-Europe handover often resets the working range
Repeated extension with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure that would lift Tail

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Tail nudges up modestly as fresh regional participation arrives and index futures begin to absorb European rate and energy moves. This reflects an expected liquidity effect, not evidence of directional structure at this hour.
